kachina-trail.note: No closures or advisories specific to this trail were found today, confirmed via the Coconino National Forest alerts page, which does not name it among any current closure orders (Source: Coconino National Forest). Coconino National Forest's Stage 2 fire restrictions remain in effect forest-wide through September 30, 2026. A Flood Watch is in effect for Coconino County from midnight tonight through 5am tomorrow for potential flash flooding from multiple rounds of thunderstorms moving through late tonight into Wednesday night (Source: National Weather Service). Afternoon and overnight monsoon thunderstorms are likely on the San Francisco Peaks; start early and avoid exposed ridgelines during storms.

walnut-canyon.note: The Island Trail's current status could not be confirmed today; the National Park Service's dedicated alerts and conditions page for Walnut Canyon National Monument again returned only stale content with no current-year update during today's check, so this trail is marked restricted out of caution until confirmed (Source: National Park Service, unconfirmed today). Historical NPS guidance states the Island Trail closes only during an active Red Flag Warning; no Red Flag Warning is currently active anywhere in Arizona today, confirmed via the National Weather Service active alerts feed (Source: National Weather Service). This would suggest the trail is open under that stated policy, but it has not been directly confirmed against a current park alert page. A Flood Watch is in effect for Coconino County from midnight tonight through 5am tomorrow for potential flash flooding from multiple rounds of thunderstorms moving through late tonight into Wednesday night (Source: National Weather Service). Call the monument at 928-526-3367 to confirm access before visiting.

lava-river-cave.note: FR 171, the access road from FR 245 to the Lava River Cave trailhead, remains open; no closure order for FR 171 appears on the Coconino National Forest alerts page today (Source: Coconino National Forest). Coconino National Forest's Stage 2 fire restrictions remain in effect forest-wide through September 30, 2026. A Flood Watch is in effect for Coconino County from midnight tonight through 5am tomorrow for potential flash flooding from multiple rounds of thunderstorms moving through late tonight into Wednesday night (Source: National Weather Service). The cave itself is unlit and near freezing year round; bring multiple light sources and sturdy footwear.

fossil-springs.note: A parking permit ($6 per vehicle via Recreation.gov) remains required April 1 through October 1, 2026 for the Fossil Creek corridor; permits remain available seven days a week for the rest of the 2026 season, with camping prohibited in the permit area and campfires and glass containers banned (Source: Coconino National Forest; Recreation.gov). Coconino National Forest's Stage 2 fire restrictions remain in effect forest-wide through September 30, 2026. A Flood Watch is in effect for Coconino County from midnight tonight through 5am tomorrow for potential flash flooding from multiple rounds of thunderstorms moving through late tonight into Wednesday night (Source: National Weather Service). This trail crosses Fossil Creek in a canyon, so avoid hiking it during and shortly after any storm tonight or tomorrow morning. Hike early morning and carry extra water.

south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: No change since the National Park Service expanded closures on September 3, 2026, reconfirmed unchanged today: South Kaibab Trail is open only from the trailhead to Tip-Off Point (about 4.4 miles down) and closed below that due to hazardous conditions from flash flooding (Source: National Park Service). Ooh Aah Point (0.9 miles) and Cedar Ridge (1.5 miles), the trail's popular shorter destinations, remain within the open section. This follows the severe flash flood in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29 that destroyed nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek; the park states there is no estimated reopening at this time and recovery work is continuing. This trail is fully sun exposed with no water source below the trailhead; confirm current water status at the trailhead before descending. A Flood Watch is in effect for Coconino County from midnight tonight through 5am tomorrow for potential flash flooding from multiple rounds of thunderstorms moving through late tonight into Wednesday night (Source: National Weather Service). The Grand Canyon area is included in that watch; the National Park Service continues to warn that additional thunderstorms could bring further flash flooding, debris flows, and rockfall in the inner canyon with little to no warning. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park; National Weather Service.

bright-angel-indian-garden.note: No change since the National Park Service expanded closures on September 3, 2026, reconfirmed unchanged today: Bright Angel Trail remains open only from the trailhead to Havasupai Gardens (formerly Indian Garden) at the Tonto Trail intersection; the trail is closed below that intersection except for river-trip exchanges at Pipe Creek Beach (Source: National Park Service). This follows the severe flash flood in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29 that closed Phantom Ranch, the North Kaibab Trail, and the river-crossing bridges; the park states recovery is ongoing with no estimated reopening at this time. Stage 4 water restrictions remain in effect; most inner-canyon water sources are off, though South Kaibab Trailhead water remains on, and Grand Canyon National Park separately advises day hikers descend no farther than 1.5 miles from the upper trailhead due to elevated Inner Canyon heat risk regardless of warning status. A Flood Watch is in effect for Coconino County from midnight tonight through 5am tomorrow for potential flash flooding from multiple rounds of thunderstorms moving through late tonight into Wednesday night (Source: National Weather Service). The National Park Service continues to warn that additional thunderstorms could bring further flash flooding and debris flows in the inner canyon. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park; National Weather Service.

rim-trail.note: No closures reported today; the Rim Trail is not affected by the Bright Angel Canyon flash flood closure, reconfirmed unchanged today (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). A Flood Watch is in effect for Coconino County from midnight tonight through 5am tomorrow for potential flash flooding from multiple rounds of thunderstorms moving through late tonight into Wednesday night (Source: National Weather Service). Use caution near the rim during any lightning.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: The entirety of North Kaibab Trail, Phantom Ranch (including Bright Angel Campground, the Canteen, and cabins), and the Black Bridge and Silver Bridge river crossings remain closed with no estimated reopening, reconfirmed unchanged today (Source: National Park Service). The closure follows the severe flash flood that struck Bright Angel Canyon on August 29, destroying nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek and damaging the Transcanyon pipeline that supplies South Rim water. Phantom Ranch reservations remain cancelled and Colorado River traffic through the area remains halted. Park recovery crews are continuing infrastructure assessment and repair work, including a temporary water intake at Bright Angel Creek; the park says this work is expected to take weeks, not months. A Flood Watch is in effect for Coconino County from midnight tonight through 5am tomorrow for potential flash flooding from multiple rounds of thunderstorms moving through late tonight into Wednesday night (Source: National Weather Service). The National Park Service continues to warn that additional thunderstorms could bring further flash flooding, debris flows, and rockfall with little to no warning. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park; National Weather Service.
